data.narrative:
Layup Parts is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zack Eakin that has raised $2M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader robotics and manufacturing peer universe of nine private companies and one public comparable (277810.KQ), though only one same-stage peer exists with sufficient data density for direct comparison.

Given the limited same-stage peer set, the Stage-Progression method was the primary applicable triangulation approach. This method applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage transitions to a $42M total-raised proxy baseline, yielding an implied valuation of $105M. The peer-median approach was not viable due to insufficient narrow comparables—while eight robotics and manufacturing peers exist in the broader universe, filtering by stage and valuation tier produced fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide medians unreliable.

The triangulated range is $89M (low) to $121M (high), with a median of $105M. This single-method result carries meaningful uncertainty: the analysis relies entirely on stage-progression mechanics rather than market-validated peer multiples. Key uncertainties include the stability of typical seed step-up multiples in the current robotics subsector, the relevance of the broader sector peer set given limited narrow comparables, and whether the $42M proxy adequately represents Layup Parts' operational footprint at seed stage. Additional revenue, customer, or product-stage data would materially strengthen conviction in this range.
